analysis:
The supplied units are base_text excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md (base lines 4071-4930). The changed ranges in the file_changes patch fall outside those excerpts (head ~3528-3536, 5230-5294), so I could not examine the changed text directly. The patch excerpt is truncated and incomplete.

The patch is documentation only. It makes four changes:
- It bumps the 'Last updated' date.
- It describes the cluster service heartbeat. DARKBLOOM_CLUSTER_MEMBER_HEALTH_FILE names the file, ClusterServiceAgent.healthPath is service-health.json, and the supervisor's liveness guard accepts only a beat with the service's own PID. A coordinator-paired part gets a separate part-health.json via partEnvironment, so it cannot overwrite the service heartbeat.
- It states that signed releases compute and register cluster_runtime approval digests from their final app, and that guided setup matches a served approval with the same computation.
- It adds links.

No code, auth, crypto or config is changed in this PR as supplied. The base excerpts I did see (cluster KV quantization, SSD prefix record encoding, GPT-OSS/MiMo batching, manifest pins) are unchanged context. They are consistent with existing fail-closed behavior: load agreement checks, authenticated-record binding, and encoding sealed in record headers. The prefix-cache material relates to T-041 (encrypted SSD tier, HMAC names, TTL). I found nothing in the visible text that widens that exposure.

Open integration questions are:
- The health-file split and the release-computed cluster_runtime digests are documented but not implemented here. The code in ClusterServiceAgent, ClusterService.partEnvironment and the release lane was not supplied, so I cannot confirm that it matches the docs. The same applies to the PID-bound liveness check and the digest binding.
- The docs claim release-computed digests replace manually typed approvals. Whether the cluster admission trust still rests on an independent qualification (A-017, T-054) depends on code outside this PR.

No finding is raised. The only residual uncertainty is that the implementation changes behind these doc updates were not supplied.
